note: A family groups occurrences that share a canonical core ask. Families key on (question_id, limb_label) because three of the four families below recur at LIMB level, not question level. Dormancy is stated only where the evidence supports it; where MIW's holdings floor at January 2021 makes dormancy unknowable, it is declared INSUFFICIENT_DATA rather than computed from a window that does not exist.

dormancy_classes.ACTIVE_RECURRENCE: appeared in 2 or more sittings within the last 24 months
dormancy_classes.RECENT_RETURN: previous appearance 24-48 months before the current sitting
dormancy_classes.LONG_DORMANT_REVIVAL: previous KNOWN appearance more than 48 months before, with the gap evidenced rather than assumed
dormancy_classes.ONE_OFF_HISTORICAL: exactly one known prior appearance and no pattern
dormancy_classes.INSUFFICIENT_DATA: the corpus cannot support a dormancy claim

threshold_justification: The 24/48-month cuts follow the sitting calendar, not statistics: MEO Class I sits ~11 times a year, so 24 months is ~22 sittings - long enough that a candidate preparing from recent papers would still have met the question, and 48 months is roughly a full preparation generation. These are proposed, not settled. The far more important rule is the last class: MIW's evidence floor is January 2021, so any 'dormant since 2012' claim is really 'not seen in the window MIW can see'. Phase 1 refuses to dress that absence up as dormancy.

families.canonical_core_ask: State the preparations and trials required to bring a ship out of a major lay-up and offer it to the surveying authorities.
families.dormancy_gap: 14 years 1 month between the two KNOWN occurrences
families.dormancy_caveat: The gap is a gap in EVIDENCE as much as in examining. MIW holds nothing between 2012 and 2021, and DieselShip's 2013-2020 sets are gated. The question may well have been set in that window. Do not tell a candidate it was 'not asked for 14 years'.
families.limb_note: Recurs at limb (a) only. Limb (b), on how a laid-up notation affects intermediate, annual and special surveys, has no located ancestor and is 6 of the 16 marks.
families.related_miw_family: MIW's own six-year layer holds a lay-up family (QP2101-Q4, QP2107-Q1, QP2109-Q1, QP2110-Q5, QP2111-Q5, QP2206-Q5) which sets the INVERSE question - preservation of machinery going INTO lay-up. That is a different question and is not counted as an occurrence here.

families.canonical_core_ask: State the coordination and exchange of information with the Master necessary for a vessel entering dry dock.
families.dormancy_gap: 14 years 1 month between the two KNOWN occurrences
families.dormancy_caveat: Same evidence caveat as FAMILY-EM-0001. MIW additionally holds a nearer relative twice - QP2109-Q3 and QP2110-Q9 both set 'explain how you will prepare vessel for dry docking' - which covers the PREPARATION limb and shows the topic was live in 2021.
families.limb_note: The historical question IS the modern question's first limb, near-verbatim. The modern question then adds delegation of responsibilities to the engineers, and inspections and co-operation with the dock authorities for UNDOCKING. Roughly two thirds of the 16 marks have no ancestor. Classifying the whole question as NEAR_VERBATIM would materially mislead a candidate.

families.canonical_core_ask: As Chief Engineer, address lack of motivation, differences in attitude, and the sense of competitiveness, for better management and effective control.
families.dormancy_caveat: Earliest KNOWN appearance is March 2021 only because that is MIW's evidence floor. The Founder hypothesis places it at March 2010; that could not be tested (see verification/H5).
families.limb_note: This is the strongest and cleanest recurrence in the paper and the only EXACT_REPEAT. It is nevertheless a LIMB: every earlier appearance pairs the sentence with 'Explain Abraham Maslow's theory of motivation' and carries 16 marks. In August 2026 the Maslow limb is absent and the limb carries 6 marks. A candidate told 'Q8 is a repeat' would over-prepare Maslow and under-prepare limb (a), which is the 10-mark PSC/communication limb and is NOT a repeat.
families.answer_donor: QP2512-Q4 is solved and carries a verified MIW answer for this limb.

families.canonical_core_ask: Explain warranties under the Marine Insurance Act.
families.dormancy_caveat: Related MIW occurrences are QP2102-Q8 and QP2202-Q8 (how many types of warranty), and QP2312-Q3(b) and QP2606-Q3(b) (differentiate express and implied warranties with a hull and machinery example). These are recorded here as family members but are not separately serialised as occurrence objects in Phase 1.
families.limb_note: Only limb (b) of four recurs - 4 of 16 marks. The command also weakens: earlier appearances say 'differentiate ... with an example', August 2026 says 'write short notes'. Limbs (a) Deviation, (c) War Risk Clause and (d) Charterers Contribution Clause have no ancestor anywhere in MIW's holdings, and (d) in particular is the least-supported limb in the whole paper.

excluded_from_families: QP2608-Q3, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q9 - no EXACT/NEAR/SAME-CORE ancestor located. Topic relationships exist and are recorded in each question's recurrence_adjudication in the spec, but a topic relationship is not a family.
